lines.gloss: Mind-preceded [are] dhammā (mental states / phenomena),

witness_glosses.zh: Mind is the root (basis) of dharmas (法),
witness_glosses.bo: Mind goes before dharmas (ཆོས),

differences.note: 本 'root/basis' renders pubbaṅgama 'going before' as 'mind is the basis of'; same Indic sense, causal priority stated as a root.

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses agree in sense; the rendering of dhammā (and zh 法, bo ཆོས) must be fixed once for the book.

lines.gloss: mind-chief, mind-made.

witness_glosses.zh: mind is honoured (supreme), mind commands / causes (心使).
witness_glosses.bo: mind is swift, mind is chief.

differences.note: Pāli manomayā 'made of / made by mind' against -javā 'swift' in Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan (ཡིད་མགྱོགས 'mind-swift'); Patna here sides against the Pāli.
心使 'mind commands/causes' is ambiguous: it fits 'mind-made' (mind as the agent) better than 'swift', but it may be a free rendering; not decisive.
Tibetan reverses the two epithets (swift, then chief).

lines.tier_reason: Real difference of sense with Pāli alone (perhaps plus an ambiguous Chinese) against Patna, Gāndhārī and the Udānavarga; a lineage-count rule settles it, but the line is famous and the owner may wish to see it.

lines.gloss: If with a corrupted (malign) mind

witness_glosses.zh: [If] in the heart one thinks evil,
witness_glosses.bo: If with a very malicious mind

differences.note: hi 'for/indeed' instead of conditional ce; Patna ca can stand for ce; Tibetan གལ་ཏེ 'if' agrees with Pāli. The English 'if/when' covers both.
中心念惡 'inwardly the mind thinks evil' renders paduṭṭha as thinking evil; same sense.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense in all witnesses; ce/hi is a grammar-neutral particle difference.

lines.gloss: one speaks or acts,

witness_glosses.zh: then speaks, then acts,
witness_glosses.bo: whether one speaks or acts,

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses agree.

lines.gloss: from that suffering follows him,

witness_glosses.zh: wrongdoing and suffering pursue [him] of themselves,
witness_glosses.bo: by that he obtains suffering,

differences.note: 罪苦 adds 'wrongdoing/guilt' to suffering; 自追 'pursue of themselves' = follows.
འཐོབ 'obtains' for anveti 'follows'; Sanskrit has anveti, so this is a Tibetan rendering matter.

lines.tier_reason: Indic witnesses identical in sense; Chinese and Tibetan render the same sense.

lines.gloss: as the wheel [follows] the foot of the one drawing [the cart].

witness_glosses.ga: as the wheel ... vahaṇe pathi (parse uncertain: 'on the track/path of the draught animal'?)
witness_glosses.zh: [as] the cart rolls over (presses into) the rut;
witness_glosses.bo: as a wheel cuts off a head.

differences.note: Tibetan 'like a wheel cutting off a head' (འཁོར་ལོས་མགོ་བོ་བཅད་པ) differs from its own Sanskrit source (cakraṁ vā vahataḥ padam); a Tibetan translation/recension matter.
車轢于轍 'cart crushing in the rut' keeps the wheel-follows image but drops the ox's foot; paraphrase.
vahaṇe pathi may mean 'on the path' rather than 'the foot'; I cannot parse it with confidence.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli, Patna and Sanskrit agree on the ox-foot simile; the Tibetan departure from its own Sanskrit and the Chinese paraphrase are settled by general rules.

verses.notes: Verse-final simile (wheel following the ox's foot) stands on pi/pd/sa; bo 'head-cutting wheel' is a Tibetan-internal divergence (Toh 326 note calls it recensional). Line 2 manomayā vs manojavā is the substantive variant.

witness_glosses.zh: Mind is the root of dharmas,
witness_glosses.bo: Mind goes before dharmas,

lines.tier_reason: As verse 1: agreement in sense; dhammā rendering is a book-wide ruling.

念善 'thinks good' renders pasanna broadly as 'good'.

witness_glosses.zh: then speaks, then acts,

lines.gloss: like a shadow that does not depart.

witness_glosses.sa: like a shadow that indeed follows.
witness_glosses.zh: like a shadow following the body (form).
witness_glosses.bo: like a shadow that follows after.

differences.note: anapāyinī 'not departing' (Pāli, Patna) vs anugāminī 'following' (Gāndhārī aṇukamiṇi, Sanskrit, Tibetan རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བ, Chinese 隨形). Same image, different word; three independent lineages against Pāli+Patna.

lines.tier_reason: Same image but a different word, with Pāli+Patna against Gāndhārī, Udānavarga and Chinese; the lineage-count rule (or the wording ruling) settles it.

verses.notes: Watch the verse-final simile: 'not departing' vs 'following'.

lines.gloss: 'He abused me, he struck me,

witness_glosses.zh: If someone reviles me,
witness_glosses.bo: '[He] spoke harshly to me, reviled [me]' (syntax of ཁ་ཟེར་བ་དག་ལ་གཤེ uncertain; dag may mark plural)

differences.note: avadhi 'struck' (Pāli, Patna) vs verbal abuse only: Sanskrit avocan 'spoke', Tibetan ཁ་ཟེར/གཤེ 'scold/revile', Chinese (T212) 罵 'revile'.
Chinese is T212 (Chuyao jing), an Udānavarga-family text, so it is not independent of sa/bo; it is phrased as a condition ('if someone').
Forms ākrośan/avocan are plural or participial; the comparative edition marks 'm avocan mām' as editorial (ins), so the Sanskrit wording here may be partly restored.

lines.tier_reason: A real sense difference (physical vs verbal assault) split Pāli+Patna against the Udānavarga family, with the Gāndhārī absent; no lineage majority.

lines.gloss: he defeated me, he robbed me' —

witness_glosses.sa: he defeated me, he made [me] lose (deprived me; ajāpayet)
witness_glosses.zh: defeated me, [I] did not win,
witness_glosses.bo: 'I was defeated, he defeated me' — thus

differences.note: ajāpayet (causative of ji, 'cause to lose, deprive') ≈ ahāsi 'robbed'; my parse of ajāpayet is from Pāli jāpeti and is not certain.
Tibetan and Chinese render both verbs as defeat (བདག་ཕམ…ཕམ་བྱེད; 勝我不勝), losing 'robbed'; plausibly a rendering of the causative of ji.

lines.tier_reason: Indic witnesses probably agree (robbed ≈ deprived), but the Udānavarga-family translations read 'defeated' twice; a general rule (translations of the Uv cannot outweigh Indic agreement) settles it.

lines.gloss: those who bind it up (harbour that [thought]),

witness_glosses.zh: those who go along with gratified feeling (快意從者; sense uncertain),
witness_glosses.bo: whoever holds this in mind,

differences.note: tāni 'these' (plural object) for taṁ 'it'.
atra 'here/in this case' added; no object pronoun.
快意從者 is hard to parse; it may mean 'those who indulge [these feelings]' (≈ harbour) or something else. Low confidence.
Singular 'whoever' (གང) for plural ye.

lines.tier_reason: Indic and Tibetan agree; the Chinese line cannot be parsed with confidence, so uncertainty moves it up under the Chinese-paraphrase rule.

lines.gloss: their enmity is not appeased.

witness_glosses.zh: enmity in the end does not cease.
witness_glosses.bo: his enmity will not be pacified.

differences.note: Singular 'his' (དེ་ཡི) following singular 'whoever'.

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses agree.

verses.notes: Gāndhārī not located. Chinese fallback T212 15.7 belongs to the Udānavarga family; count it with sa/bo. Line 1 'struck' vs 'spoke' is an even split (T4).

lines.gloss: 'He abused me, he struck me,

witness_glosses.zh: If someone heaps slander and abuse,
witness_glosses.bo: '[He] spoke harshly to me, reviled [me]'

differences.note: As verse 3: struck vs verbal abuse (zh T213 毀罵 'slander and revile').
Chinese T213 14.10 is a qualified (partial) parallel from the Udānavarga-family Faji yaosong jing.

lines.tier_reason: Same even split as verse 3 line 1; decide together.

lines.gloss: he defeated me, he robbed me' —

witness_glosses.sa: he defeated me, he made [me] lose
witness_glosses.zh: he won, I did not win,
witness_glosses.bo: 'I was defeated, he defeated me' — thus

differences.note: As verse 3: 'defeat' twice.

lines.tier_reason: As verse 3 line 2.

lines.gloss: those who do not bind it up (do not harbour it),

witness_glosses.pd: those who do not harbour these [things],
witness_glosses.sa: those who here do not harbour [it],
witness_glosses.zh: one who gladly follows [his] mind (快樂從意者; no negative)
witness_glosses.bo: whoever does not hold this in mind,

differences.note: The partial Chinese parallel has no negative and does not say 'do not harbour'; its sense is uncertain.
tāni plural object, as verse 3.

lines.tier_reason: Indic and Tibetan agree on the negative; only a partial Chinese parallel differs, which informs but cannot supply the line.

lines.gloss: in them enmity is appeased.

witness_glosses.zh: enmity in the end comes to rest.
witness_glosses.bo: his enmity will be pacified.

differences.note: Genitive tesaṁ/teṣāṁ 'their' vs Pāli locative tesu 'in them'; sa pra- for upa-; same sense.

lines.gloss: For not by enmity [are] enmities

witness_glosses.zh: Those who are resentful toward enmity (the hostile),
witness_glosses.bo: Here, by enmity, those with enmity (the hostile)

differences.note: 慍於怨者 personalises: 'one who resents enmity/the enemy'; the proposition (answering enmity with resentment does not end it) is kept.
འཁོན་ཅན 'possessors of enmity' for vairāṇi 'enmities'; Tibetan rendering.

lines.tier_reason: Same proposition in all witnesses; Chinese and Tibetan render it with persons as subject.

lines.gloss: are ever appeased here;

witness_glosses.zh: have never been without enmity;
witness_glosses.bo: are never pacified;

lines.tier_reason: All agree (the negative of line 1 governs).

lines.gloss: and by non-enmity they are appeased:

witness_glosses.pd: but by non-enmity they are appeased:
witness_glosses.zh: not being resentful, [it] removes itself:
witness_glosses.bo: by patience enmity is pacified:

differences.note: kṣāntyā / བཟོད་པས 'by patience' against avera 'non-enmity' (Pāli, Patna) and Chinese 不慍 'not resenting'. Sanskrit+Tibetan are one voice.

lines.tier_reason: The Udānavarga (one lineage) stands against Pāli, Patna and Chinese; the lineage-count rule settles it.

lines.gloss: this is the eternal (age-old) dhamma.

witness_glosses.zh: this Way (道) may be honoured as a model.
witness_glosses.bo: this is the nature of dharma (ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན).

differences.note: 道 for dhamma and 可宗 'can be taken as principle' in place of sanantano; native vocabulary.
རང་བཞིན 'nature' renders sanātana; 'the nature of dharma' rather than 'eternal law'.

lines.tier_reason: Indic witnesses agree; the English for dhamma and for sanantano (eternal vs age-old) are book-wide word decisions.

verses.notes: Gāndhārī not located. zh 道 for dhamma is a native rendering covered by the dhamma ruling.

lines.gloss: Others do not understand

witness_glosses.zh: Do not like to blame others,
witness_glosses.bo: since the others do not understand,

differences.note: Partial Chinese parallel says 'do not be fond of blaming others'; different statement.
Partial Tibetan parallel (Tib. 14.8) has the same clause ཕ་རོལ་པོ་དག་མི་ཤེས་པས, in a different stanza.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna agree; the partial parallels inform only, one agreeing and one differing.

lines.gloss: that we here must restrain ourselves (or: that we here are perishing; yamāmase);

witness_glosses.pd: we here are conquering (?) (jayāmatha; sense uncertain)
witness_glosses.zh: strive to examine oneself,
witness_glosses.bo: I strive in this,

differences.note: Patna jayāmatha does not obviously mean 'restrain' or 'perish'; it may be a corruption or a different verb ('conquer'). I cannot parse it securely.
Both partial parallels speak of striving/self-examination (務自省身; བརྩོན་པར་བྱེད), which could reflect a reading 'we must strive' (yat-) rather than yam- 'restrain' or Yama 'die'.

lines.tier_reason: A known lexical crux (yamāmase: restrain vs perish), with a divergent Patna verb and partial parallels pointing to 'strive'; needs its own judgment.

witness_glosses.zh: if there is one who knows this,
witness_glosses.bo: whoever here are wise,

differences.note: 'the wise' (མཁས་པ) for 'those who understand'; close in sense.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna agree and both partial parallels are compatible.

witness_glosses.zh: [it] is forever extinguished, without trouble.
witness_glosses.bo: they are pacified by gentle words (བཞམས་པའི་ཚིག; gloss of བཞམས་པ uncertain).

medhakā for medhagā; same word ('quarrels', per PED medhaga).

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna agree; partial parallels differ and cannot supply the line; the meaning of medhagā ('quarrels') is standard but worth noting.

extra.gloss: You are of unwise (unskilled) ways, and
extra.note: Opening of the partial Tibetan stanza; no Pāli counterpart.

verses.notes: Only Pāli and Patna are full witnesses; Gāndhārī and Sanskrit not located; zh (T210 9.6) and bo (Tib. 14.8, not in Rockhill's concordance) are partial. Line 2 is a T4 crux.

candidates.label: dhamma-rendering
candidates.statement: Fix the English for dhamma/dhammā across the book, distinguishing (a) the plural dhammā of Dhp 1–2 (objects of mind / mental states / phenomena), (b) dhamma as teaching or principle (Dhp 5, 20), and how to treat the Chinese 法/道 and Tibetan ཆོས renderings (道 'the Way' is a native rendering, not a separate reading).
candidates.recommendation: Translate the plural dhammā by sense ('mental states' or 'experiences', one fixed choice), keep 'Dhamma' (capitalised, untranslated) for the teaching, and 'principle' only where the line is clearly a maxim (Dhp 5, decided with sanantano); treat 道 as agreement.

candidates.label: sanantano
candidates.statement: Rendering of sanantano / sanātana (Dhp 5 'esa dhammo sanantano'). Literal 'eternal' asserts eternity; 'age-old/ancient' asserts antiquity. Tibetan ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན 'the nature of dharma' and Chinese 可宗 'worthy to be honoured' do not decide it.
candidates.recommendation: 'age-old' (or 'ancient'): it is the commonest sense of sanātana and avoids importing metaphysics the line need not state.

candidates.label: subha-asubha
candidates.statement: English for subha / asubha in 'subhānupassī / asubhānupassī' (Dhp 7–8), also relevant elsewhere (e.g. Dhp 349–350). Witnesses: Chinese 淨 / 不淨 'pure / impure' with 身 'body' added; Tibetan གཙང / མི་གཙང 'clean / unclean'.
candidates.recommendation: 'attractive / unattractive' (literal, keeps the meditation sense without the Chinese 'body' gloss).

candidates.label: kasava-pun
candidates.statement: How to carry the pun anikkasāva / kāsāva (stain, impurity vs ochre/saffron robe) in Dhp 9–10, and the fixed English for kāsāva. Chinese (毒態 / 法衣) and Tibetan (སྙིགས་མ / ངུར་སྨྲིག) do not keep the pun.
options: Keep a pun ('still stained ... the stained robe')
Translate plainly ('not free of impurities ... the ochre robe') and let the pun go
Plain translation plus a bracketed ⟨supplied⟩ hint
candidates.recommendation: Plain literal sense with an English echo where natural ('stains' / 'stained robe'), otherwise plain; fix kāsāva = 'ochre robe' throughout.

candidates.label: samhita
candidates.statement: Meaning of saṁhita / sahita in Dhp 19–20 ('even if reciting much/little saṁhita'). Readings: 'the collection (of scriptures)' vs 'what is beneficial / meaningful (speech)'; Tibetan རིགས་བཅས 'reasoned, fitting'; Chinese paraphrases (巧言 / 時言).
candidates.recommendation: 'the teachings / scripture' with bhāsamāna as 'reciting', since the contrast with practice is the point; apply identically to both verses.

candidates.label: glossary-recurring-terms
candidates.statement: One ruling fixing the English of recurring technical terms that occur in this chapter and throughout the book: indriya, sīla, saṅkappa (and gocara), rāga / dosa / moha, puñña, pamatta, sāmañña, bhāvita / subhāvita, duggati / suggati. Lines that differ only in these renderings sit at T2 until the glossary is approved.
options: rāga, dosa, moha: passion/lust/greed, hatred/aversion, delusion
candidates.recommendation: senses; virtue; intention (with gocara 'range' / 'pasture'); passion, hatred, delusion; merit; heedless; recluseship (or 'the contemplative life'); developed; bad/good destination.

candidates.label: wording-variants
candidates.statement: Near-synonym or wording substitutions that keep the same idea but would change the English word (e.g. Sanskrit nityam for viharantam, sthiram for parvatam, praśocati for vihaññati; Gāndhārī -vādin for -mati; -saññin vs -dassin; śrāmaṇyārtha vs sāmañña; anugāminī vs anapāyinī). Synonyms that give the same English (modati/nandati, samativijjhati/samatibhindati) count as agreement (T1).
options: Follow the word with the widest independent support (lineage count); on a tie keep the Pāli word
Always keep the Pāli word for same-idea differences
candidates.recommendation: Follow the widest independent support; on a tie keep the Pāli word. (This gives 'following' for the shadow in Dhp 2, and keeps 'afflicted', 'mountain', 'recluseship'.)

candidates.label: lineage-concord
candidates.statement: Count lineages, not columns. One voice each: Pāli; Patna (weak when it agrees with Pāli); Gāndhārī (weak alone when fragmentary); Udānavarga = Sanskrit + Tibetan + the Udānavarga-family Chinese fallbacks T212 / T213; Chinese T210. A reading carried by a single voice yields to a different reading shared by at least two other independent voices. Where Pāli+Patna stand against Gāndhārī+Udānavarga on a real difference of sense, with no other decisive witness, the line is an even split and goes to T4.
options: As stated (single voice yields; Pāli+Patna vs Gāndhārī+Udānavarga = T4)
Always keep the Pāli unless every other witness agrees against it
Follow the majority of lineages including ties broken toward the Gāndhārī as oldest
candidates.recommendation: As stated. In this chapter it yields: 'swift' for manomayā (Dhp 1–2, owner may want to confirm given its fame), 'following' shadow (2), keep 'non-enmity' (5), keep 'lazy, low in energy' (7) and 'faithful' (8), keep 'undeveloped / developed' (13–14); and sends 'struck' vs 'spoke' (3–4), Māra vs passion (7–8) and truth vs gentleness (9–10) to T4.

candidates.label: tibetan-vs-sanskrit
candidates.statement: Where the Tibetan Udānavarga departs from the Sanskrit Udānavarga (e.g. 'wheel cutting off a head' for the ox-foot simile in Dhp 1; 'defeated' for the causative of ji in Dhp 3–4; mind as subject 'overcome by desires' in Dhp 13–14), treat it as a Tibetan translation or recension matter: it does not count as an independent witness against the Sanskrit and the other traditions, and it does not raise the line above T3.
options: Treat as Tibetan-internal (follow Sanskrit for the Udānavarga voice)
Treat Tibetan as a separate voice
candidates.recommendation: Treat as Tibetan-internal; note it in provenance.

candidates.label: chinese-paraphrase
candidates.statement: The Chinese (T210 and fallbacks) often paraphrases and uses native vocabulary. Where it renders the same Indic sense, it counts as agreement (T1). Where it changes an image or proposition (grass for a weak tree; 'when doing / afterwards' for 'here / after death'; 'not the Buddha's disciple' for 'no share in recluseship'; added 'body'), it is evidence of an early reading but does not by itself override agreeing Indic witnesses; the line stays at T3 and keeps the Indic sense. Unparseable Chinese lines are flagged low-confidence at T3.
options: Treat Chinese differences as variants counting as a full voice

candidates.label: partial-and-fragmentary
candidates.statement: A partial parallel (status 'partial': Chinese T213 at Dhp 4, Chinese and Tibetan at Dhp 6) or a fragmentary line (Patna at Dhp 8, 16) may confirm a reading but cannot supply or override one. Where only partial witnesses differ, the line is T3 and follows the full witnesses; lacunae are not restored from Pāli.

candidates.label: missing-lines-structure
candidates.statement: The Blend keeps the Pāli line structure. A Pāli line absent from shorter recensions (Gāndhārī and Udānavarga four-line forms of Dhp 20; Tibetan formulaic versions of Dhp 17–18) is kept when supported by Pāli and at least one other witness, or when the Pāli is unopposed by any Indic witness; absence elsewhere is recorded, not treated as contrary evidence. Line order differences in Chinese/Tibetan are ignored.
options: Drop lines absent from the majority of witnesses
